financials_interim.notes: Ceylon Tobacco Company PLC (CTC), single-entity company (no subsidiaries; manufactures/markets/sells cigarettes only), FYE 31 December. GROUP basis used per convention for single-entity filer. Q2 2026 (three months ended 30 June 2026) vs Q2 2025 (three months ended 30 June 2025) comparative -- both columns explicitly presented on the face P&L (page 3), so this is a genuine same-quarter YoY compare. revenue=16,565 is the filing's own 'Revenue' subtotal, i.e. Turnover (52,435) LESS Government Levies/excise (35,870) -- CTC presents gross Turnover and nets off Government Levies before arriving at 'Revenue', standard treatment for an excise-heavy tobacco company; Turnover itself actually FELL 4.9% YoY (52,435 vs 55,135) while Government Levies fell 6.0% (35,870 vs 38,155), netting to a smaller 2.4% decline in Revenue (16,565 vs 16,980). operating_profit=13,317 is NOT a printed subtotal -- the face P&L jumps straight from opex lines to 'Net finance income' to 'Profit before income tax'; derived here as PBT (13,624) less Net finance income (307) = 13,317, which ties to Revenue+Other operating income-Raw material-Employee benefit-D&A-Other operating expenses (16,565+9-913-1,135-180-1,029=13,317). finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- the filing only discloses a single NET 'Net finance income' line (307 for the quarter) with no gross split at the 3-month-column level (the 6-month cash flow statement shows separate interest income/expense of 587/-7 for the half year, not reconcilable to a clean 3-month split). cost_of_sales/gross_profit left blank -- no such subtotal is presented (CTC's format goes Revenue -> individual opex lines -> Profit before tax directly). shares_in_issue=187,323,751 per Note 7/9 (20 Largest Shareholders / public holding computation). short_term_borrowings=0 and long_term_borrowings=0 -- balance sheet explicitly shows 'Long term borrowings -' (dash) and no short-term borrowings line at all in current liabilities (only lease liabilities of 87 current/4 non-current, trade payables, income tax liabilities, unclaimed dividends) -- CTC carries no interest-bearing debt, confirmed by net finance INCOME (not cost) of Rs.307mn for the quarter, funded by its Rs.25,310mn cash pile. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: cash_from_operations/capex/cash_from_investing/cash_from_financing are the filing's 6-MONTHS ended 30 June 2026 CUMULATIVE figures (7,299 / -50 / -50 / -13,306), NOT quarterly -- CTC's cash flow statement is only presented on a 6-month YTD basis (page 6), with no quarterly-only breakout disclosed, unlike the income statement which does give a clean 3-month column. All other fields (income statement, balance sheet) are genuinely for the 3-month quarter / period-end position respectively. Identity check: total_liabilities (34,233) + total_equity (10,812) = 45,045 = total_assets, ties exactly. PBT (13,624) - tax (5,930) = 7,694 = PAT, ties exactly. EPS 41.07 = 7,694mn / 187.324mn shares = 41.07, ties. No segmental note in this filing -- CTC has a single reportable business (cigarette manufacturing/marketing), no segment disclosure required or given.

thesis.thesis_text: Ceylon Tobacco Company, Sri Lanka's dominant legal cigarette manufacturer and a British American Tobacco subsidiary, reported Q2 2026 PAT of Rs.7.69bn, +4.5% YoY, even as Revenue (net of Government Levies) fell 2.4% to Rs.16.57bn and gross Turnover fell 4.9% -- the PAT growth came almost entirely from a 43.9% (Rs.806mn) cut in Other Operating Expenses and a lower effective tax rate (43.5% vs 46.9%), not from volume or revenue growth, while raw material, employee and depreciation costs all rose well ahead of revenue (+37.5%/+50.3%/+39.5%). The company carries zero interest-bearing debt and holds a Rs.25.3bn cash pile generating net finance income, giving it an extremely strong, capital-light balance sheet, though this also produces a structurally tiny book value (Rs.10.81bn total equity) that inflates P/B to roughly 31x. At Rs.1,795.50 (31 Aug 2026) the stock trades on an estimated ~11.68x run-rate P/E (annualizing H1 2026's Rs.14.39bn cumulative PAT, +2% YoY); no dividend data exists in this database for CTC, though the interim filing itself discloses a second interim dividend of Rs.41.00/share declared, payable 14 September 2026 (Interim Financial Statements, source_doc_id 52517, p.3).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no CBSL/IMF/World Bank/news/regulatory-policy data source exists in this project, which is a particularly material gap for a tobacco company whose profit pool is directly shaped by government excise policy. The remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Only ONE interim period is on file for CTC, and unlike the four banks in this batch it is stored on a QUARTER-ONLY basis (not H1 cumulative) -- the P/E here was estimated by annualizing the filing's separately-disclosed H1 2026 cumulative PAT (Rs.14.39bn) rather than the quarterly figure, but this remains a run-rate approximation, not a true TTM, and no annual report has been reviewed. No dividend data exists in this database's dividends table for CTC at all, despite the interim filing itself disclosing a declared second interim dividend of Rs.41.00/share -- this is a genuine data gap, not an indication CTC pays no dividend. Governance & Risk reflects standard listed-company oversight (BAT parent group) but no circulars/disclosures feed exists to verify recent governance events independently.

financial_quality.rationale: Zero interest-bearing debt (short and long-term borrowings both nil) and a Rs.25.31bn cash pile generate net finance income (Rs.307mn for the quarter, +10.0% YoY), giving CTC an exceptionally strong, capital-light balance sheet. Operating margin ~80.4% and net margin ~46.4% for Q2 2026. Implied annualized ROE is ~266% (H1 2026 PAT run-rate of Rs.28.79bn over Rs.10.81bn total equity) -- this extreme figure is a structural artefact of CTC's high-payout dividend policy leaving a deliberately thin retained-equity base, not a sign of unusual capital efficiency growth.

growth_outlook.rationale: Revenue (net of Government Levies) fell 2.4% YoY to Rs.16.57bn and gross Turnover fell 4.9% in Q2 2026; for the six months ended 30 June 2026, PAT grew only 2% to Rs.14.39bn. The quarter's headline PAT growth of +4.5% (to Rs.7.69bn) came almost entirely from a 43.9% (Rs.806mn) cut in Other Operating Expenses and a lower effective tax rate (43.5% vs 46.9%) -- not from volume or revenue growth -- while raw material (+37.5%), employee benefit (+50.3%) and depreciation (+39.5%) costs all rose well ahead of revenue. This is a declining-volume, cost-and-tax-driven earnings picture.

valuation.rationale: Estimated P/E of ~11.68x (price Rs.1,795.50 on 2026-08-31, annualizing the filing's disclosed H1 2026 cumulative PAT of Rs.14.39bn x2 = Rs.28,786mn run-rate, EPS ~Rs.153.68) is not statistically cheap like the four banks in this batch. P/B of ~31.11x (BVPS Rs.57.72 on a deliberately thin Rs.10.81bn equity base, 187,323,751 shares) is extremely high but reflects CTC's high-payout policy rather than overvaluation in the conventional sense. No dividend data exists in this database's dividends table, though the interim filing discloses a second interim dividend of Rs.41.00/share declared, payable 14 September 2026 -- a genuine data gap, not evidence of low yield.

business_quality.rationale: Dominant, near-monopoly legal cigarette manufacturer/marketer in Sri Lanka (a British American Tobacco subsidiary) with a strong brand franchise and no reportable segments outside its core business. This strong competitive position is offset by structural industry headwinds -- declining Turnover (-4.9% YoY) consistent with excise-driven pricing and/or illicit-trade competition typical of a mature, globally-declining legal tobacco market.

governance_risk.rationale: Standard listed-company governance under British American Tobacco parent-group oversight; no debt, no dilutive events, and a stable share count. CTC's entire profit pool is directly shaped by government excise/levy policy set annually (Government Levies of Rs.35.87bn in the quarter, nearly 2.2x the company's own Revenue) -- a structural policy-dependency risk with no governance/internal-controls concern identified, but a material external-policy sensitivity worth flagging given no macro/regulatory-policy data source exists in this project.

key_reasons: Fortress balance sheet: zero interest-bearing debt, Rs.25.3bn cash pile, net finance income (not expense) of Rs.307mn for the quarter -- among the strongest financial positions in this cohort
PAT still grew 4.5% YoY to Rs.7.69bn despite a 2.4% revenue decline, via disciplined cost control (Other Operating Expenses -43.9%, a Rs.806mn saving) and a lower effective tax rate (43.5% vs 46.9%)
Dominant, near-monopoly legal cigarette franchise in Sri Lanka with an ~80% operating margin and ~46% net margin -- structurally high profitability for whatever scale of business remains
A second interim dividend of Rs.41.00/share was declared per the filing itself (payable 14 Sept 2026), though no dividend history is yet captured in this database's dividends table
watch_factors: Revenue and Turnover both declined (-2.4% and -4.9% respectively) -- H1 2026 PAT growth was only +2% (Rs.14.39bn vs Rs.14.04bn), far slower than the Q2-only headline (+4.5%), and both were driven by cost cuts and tax-rate relief rather than volume/revenue growth, which may not repeat at the same magnitude

Raw material (+37.5%), employee benefit (+50.3%) and depreciation (+39.5%) costs all rose well ahead of revenue -- continued cost inflation without further offsetting 'other opex' savings would pressure margins

P/B of ~31.1x is extremely high (reflecting a deliberately thin retained-equity base from high payout policy, not overvaluation in the conventional sense) and P/E of ~11.7x is not statistically cheap like the four banks in this batch -- CTC is priced as a stable-income/dividend name, not a value opportunity

No dividend history exists in this database despite CTC being a well-known reliable dividend payer -- the yield-support component of this valuation case cannot be verified from data on file, only inferred from the interim filing's mention of a Rs.41.00/share second interim dividend

horizon_notes.6m: H2 2026 results will show whether the Rs.806mn 'other opex' saving and lower effective tax rate that drove Q2 PAT growth are repeatable, or whether declining Turnover (-4.9% YoY) starts to show through to the bottom line.
horizon_notes.1y: If revenue stabilizes and cost inflation (raw material, employee, D&A all up 35-50% YoY) is contained without further one-off opex savings, PAT growth could become more volume/revenue-driven rather than cost-driven; continued volume decline would test the current ~11.7x multiple.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether CTC can sustain its near-monopoly pricing power and margins against structural industry headwinds (excise policy, illicit trade) that are driving the observed Turnover decline.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/regulatory-policy data source in this project to assess multi-year excise/health-policy risk, which is the single largest structural variable for a tobacco company's long-run earnings power.

interim_updates.note_text: Ceylon Tobacco Company PLC (CTC) reported Profit After Tax of Rs.7,694mn for Q2 2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 4.5% YoY from Rs.7,365mn, even as Revenue (net of Government Levies) declined 2.4% to Rs.16,565mn (2025: Rs.16,980mn) -- gross Turnover fell 4.9% to Rs.52,435mn (2025: Rs.55,135mn) while Government Levies paid fell a similar 6.0% to Rs.35,870mn (2025: Rs.38,155mn). Cost pressures were evident on several specific lines: Raw material used rose 37.5% to Rs.913mn (2025: Rs.664mn), Employee benefit expense rose 50.3% to Rs.1,135mn (2025: Rs.755mn), and Depreciation & amortisation rose 39.5% to Rs.180mn (2025: Rs.129mn) -- together a Rs.680mn combined drag. This was more than offset by a 43.9% fall in Other operating expenses to Rs.1,029mn (2025: Rs.1,835mn), a Rs.806mn saving that was the single largest favourable swing in the quarter and the primary reason Profit before tax only fell 1.8% (to Rs.13,624mn from Rs.13,876mn) despite the Rs.415mn Revenue decline and Rs.680mn rise in raw material/employee/D&A costs combined. PAT growth then outpaced the modest PBT decline because Income tax expense fell 8.9% to Rs.5,930mn (2025: Rs.6,511mn) -- a larger proportionate fall than PBT, implying the effective tax rate eased to 43.5% (2025: 46.9%). Net finance income (CTC carries no debt) rose 10.0% to Rs.307mn (2025: Rs.279mn). Basic EPS rose 4.5% to Rs.41.07 (2025: Rs.39.32). For the six months ended 30 June 2026, PAT grew a more modest 2% to Rs.14,393mn (2025: Rs.14,044mn), consistent with the company's own disclosure. No segmental note is presented -- CTC operates a single cigarette manufacturing/marketing business with no reportable segments.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to 30 June 2026 has been collected for CTC -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. No segmental note is disclosed in this filing (CTC has a single reportable business, cigarette manufacturing/marketing, so no segment breakdown exists to attribute growth/decline to specific business lines). Cash flow statement figures stored in financial_statements are 6-month cumulative (only basis disclosed), not quarterly -- flagged in that row's notes field, does not affect this note's YoY figures which are all drawn from the reliable 3-month P&L/balance-sheet columns. finance_costs/finance_income are not split at the 3-month level (only a net 'Net finance income' line is given), so no gross interest income/expense YoY comparison is possible.
interim_updates.takeaway: CTC's 4.5% YoY PAT growth to Rs.7,694mn was NOT driven by volume/revenue growth -- Revenue actually fell 2.4% and PBT fell 1.8% -- but by two specific items: a 43.9% (Rs.806mn) cut in Other operating expenses (the single largest favourable swing, consistent with management's cited 'disciplined cost control measures'), and a lower effective tax rate (43.5% vs 46.9%, saving Rs.581mn) that more than offset the modest PBT decline. Underlying cost inflation is visible and worth watching: raw material (+37.5%), employee benefits (+50.3%) and D&A (+39.5%) all rose well ahead of revenue, so further PAT growth will need either a revenue recovery or continuation of the current pace of 'other opex' savings, which may not repeat at the same magnitude.

operational_highlights: Revenue (net of Government Levies) Rs.16,565mn, -2.4% YoY (2025: Rs.16,980mn); PBT Rs.13,624mn, -1.8% YoY; PAT Rs.7,694mn, +4.5% YoY.
Government revenue (levies) paid by the Company amounted to Rs.41.8bn in H1 2026, +4% YoY, per the Directors' summary of performance.
Second interim dividend of Rs.41.00 per share declared, payable 14 September 2026.
Raw material used +37.5% YoY (Rs.913mn vs Rs.664mn); Employee benefit expense +50.3% YoY (Rs.1,135mn vs Rs.755mn); Depreciation & amortisation +39.5% YoY (Rs.180mn vs Rs.129mn).

Other operating expenses fell 43.9% YoY to Rs.1,029mn (2025: Rs.1,835mn), a Rs.806mn saving -- the single largest favourable swing in the quarter, per the Directors' note on 'ongoing savings initiatives and disciplined cost control measures'.
Effective tax rate eased to 43.5% (2025: 46.9%), with tax expense falling 8.9% to Rs.5,930mn even as PBT fell only 1.8%.

Cash and cash equivalents fell to Rs.25,310mn (31 Dec 2025: Rs.31,367mn) after dividend payments of Rs.13,229mn in H1 2026 (6-month cash flow); no interest-bearing borrowings on the balance sheet (short and long-term borrowings both nil).
key_drivers: Other operating expenses fell 43.9% YoY (Rs.1,029mn vs Rs.1,835mn, a Rs.806mn reduction) -- the dominant driver preventing a larger PBT decline, more than offsetting the combined Rs.680mn rise in raw material (+37.5%), employee benefit (+50.3%) and D&A (+39.5%) costs plus the Rs.415mn Revenue decline.
Effective tax rate fell to 43.5% from 46.9% -- income tax expense dropped 8.9% (Rs.581mn) even though PBT only fell 1.8% (Rs.252mn), which is why PAT grew 4.5% despite PBT declining.

Government Levies (excise) paid fell 6.0% YoY (Rs.35,870mn vs Rs.38,155mn) roughly in line with the 4.9% fall in gross Turnover, so the levies/turnover ratio was broadly stable and not itself a swing factor in Revenue.
